statement: In pylint-linted code, functions may take more than the configured maximum number of arguments (too-many-arguments is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, pylint does not require docstrings (missing-docstring is turned off; docstrings are checked by flake8-docstrings instead).
In pylint-linted code, pylint does not check import position (wrong-import-position is turned off; handled by isort).
In pylint-linted code, the whole pylint design checker (too-many-branches, too-many-locals, too-many-instance-attributes, too-few-public-methods, etc.) is turned off.
In pylint-linted code, re-raising inside an except block without 'from' is allowed (raise-missing-from is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, methods that only delegate to super() are allowed (useless-super-delegation is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, redefining built-in names (e.g. id, type, input) is allowed (redefined-builtin is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, instance attributes may be defined outside __init__ (attribute-defined-outside-init is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, overriding methods may have a different signature from the overridden method (arguments-differ is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, standalone string statements (e.g. string-literal comments) are allowed (pointless-string-statement is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, catching broad exceptions such as 'except Exception' is allowed (broad-except is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, unnecessary 'pass' statements are allowed (unnecessary-pass is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, unresolvable imports are not reported (import-error is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, accesses to members pylint cannot infer are not reported (no-member is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, pylint does not report unused imports (unused-import is turned off; flake8 F401 handles it).

quote: disable= no-else-return, # A complete if else block can improve readability even with returns in the body
statement: In pylint-linted code, an else branch after an if branch that returns is allowed (no-else-return is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, pylint does not check import order (wrong-import-order is turned off; isort handles it).

quote:
# FIXME Refactor/cleanup cli code to solve following warnings
disable= duplicate-code
statement: In pylint-linted code, duplicated code blocks are not reported (duplicate-code is turned off pending refactoring).
In pylint-linted code, str.format() and %-formatting are allowed instead of f-strings (consider-using-f-string is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, raising the generic Exception class is allowed (broad-exception-raised is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, dict() calls are allowed instead of {} literals (use-dict-literal is turned off).
In pylint-linted code, pylint reports accesses to members of C extensions it cannot find (c-extension-no-member is explicitly enabled).
In pylint-linted code, functions must not nest more than 6 blocks deep (too-many-nested-blocks).
In pylint-linted code, local variables that are intentionally unused must be named _ , _-prefixed, dummy, ignored_* or unused_* (otherwise unused-variable is reported).
In pylint-linted code, function arguments that are intentionally unused must be named _*, ignored_*, unused_*, args or kwargs (otherwise unused-argument is reported).
In pylint-linted code, lines must not exceed 120 characters, except lines consisting only of a URL (line-too-long).
In pylint-linted code, a module must not exceed 1000 lines (too-many-lines).
In pylint-linted code, function arguments must be named in snake_case (invalid-name).
In pylint-linted code, instance attributes must be named in snake_case (invalid-name).

statement: In Python files, code must not contain debugger imports or breakpoint() calls (pdb, ipdb, etc.).
In all files, private keys must not be committed.
In all files, files marked executable must start with a shebang line.

quote: Make sure **to have added unit tests or integration tests** to cover the new/modified code.
statement: In all source changes, new or modified code must be covered by added unit tests or integration tests.

quote: Changes to the API request/response model require changes to files under `cli/src/pcluster/api/models`. The newly generated models in the server stub can be imported as is, just mind fixing unused imports and formatting. To avoid huge diffs import only models related to your modifications.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/models, API request/response models must be the OpenAPI-generated server stub models, imported as is with unused imports removed.

quote: The updated controller signature can be retrieved from the generated stub files and relevant changes need to be applied to controllers under the `cli/src/pcluster/api/controllers` directory.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/controllers, API endpoint handlers must live under this directory and match the controller signatures of the OpenAPI-generated server stub.

quote: Please import the newly changes available in the generated stub to `cli/src/pcluster/api/openapi/openapi.yaml`. For each diff with the respect to the generated file please add an `#  override: reason` comment documenting why this is required.
statement: In cli/src/pcluster/api/openapi/openapi.yaml, every deviation from the generated OpenAPI spec must carry an '# override: <reason>' comment.

quote: All integration tests are defined in the `integration-tests/tests` directory.
statement: In tests/integration-tests, integration test modules must be placed under tests/integration-tests/tests/.

quote: search for `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` files ... `test_` prefixed test functions or methods outside of class; `test_` prefixed test functions or methods inside `Test` prefixed test classes (without an `__init__` method)
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, test files must be named test_*.py or *_test.py, test functions must be prefixed test_, and test classes must be prefixed Test and have no __init__ method.

quote: Test cases are organized in separate files where the file name is `test_$feature_under_test`. For example test cases specific to awsbatch scheduler can be defined in a file named `test_awsbatch.py`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, each test file must be named test_<feature_under_test>.py, optionally grouped in a per-feature or per-category directory.

quote: If you don't need to reference the parametrized arguments in your test case you can simply replace the function arguments with this annotation: `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("region", "os", "instance", "scheduler")`
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, test functions that do not use the region/os/instance/scheduler dimension arguments should declare them with @pytest.mark.usefixtures("region", "os", "instance", "scheduler") instead of as function arguments.

quote: It is possible to restrict the dimensions each test is compatible with by using some custom markers. ... @pytest.mark.instances ... @pytest.mark.regions ... @pytest.mark.oss ... @pytest.mark.schedulers ... @pytest.mark.dimensions ... @pytest.mark.skip_*
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, restricting a test's dimensions should be done with the custom markers @pytest.mark.instances/regions/oss/schedulers/dimensions and their skip_* counterparts.

quote: To define such exceptions it is possible to extend the list `UNSUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS` in conftest_markers.py file. By default, all tuples specified in that list will be added as `skip_dimensions` markers to all tests.
statement: In tests/integration-tests, globally unsupported dimension combinations should be declared by extending UNSUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS in tests/integration-tests/conftest_markers.py rather than per-test.

quote: Tests data and resources are organized in the following directories: ... $test_file_i.py: contains resources for test cases defined in file $test_file_i.py ... $test_case_i: contains resources for test case $test_case_i ... data: contains common resources to share across all tests
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, per-test resources must be placed in <test_file_name>/<test_case_name>/ next to the test module, and resources shared across tests in tests/integration-tests/tests/data/.

quote: A fixture `test_datadir` is built on top of it and can be used to inject the `datadir` with resources for the specific test function. ... The fixture `shared_datadir` can be used similarly to access the shared resource directory.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, tests should access their per-test resources via the test_datadir fixture and shared resources via the shared_datadir fixture.

quote: The cluster configuration needed for a given test case needs to reside in the test specific `test_datadir` and it needs to be in a file named pcluster.config.yaml.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, the cluster configuration for a test case must be a file named pcluster.config.yaml inside that test case's data directory (<test_file>/<test_case>/pcluster.config.yaml).

quote: Test cases can then inject a fixture called `pcluster_config_reader` which allows to automatically read and render the configuration defined for a specific test case
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, tests should read and render their cluster configuration through the pcluster_config_reader fixture.

quote: Cluster lifecycle management is fully managed by the testing framework and is exposed through the fixture `clusters_factory`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, clusters must be created through the clusters_factory fixture so the framework manages their lifecycle and cleanup.

quote: To execute remote commands or scripts on the head node of the cluster under test, the `RemoteCommandExecutor` class can be used.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, remote commands and scripts on the cluster head node should be executed via RemoteCommandExecutor (run_remote_command / run_remote_script).

quote: If additional AWS resources are needed by the integration tests you can use a session scoped fixture, `cfn_stacks_factory`, ... (note: fixtures are always better to handle resources cleanup.)
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, additional AWS resources should be created as CloudFormation stacks via the cfn_stacks_factory fixture (or a fixture wrapping CfnStacksFactory) so cleanup is handled by fixtures.

quote: To run performance test for a specific integration test, the following changes are required: 1. Add `run_benchmarks` and `benchmarks` fixtures to the test ... 2. Add `benchmarks` parameter to `pcluster_config_reader`.
statement: In tests/integration-tests/tests, an integration test that runs performance benchmarks must take the run_benchmarks and benchmarks fixtures and pass benchmarks=benchmarks to pcluster_config_reader.
